titulo: Their clock, not the one on your phone
subtitulo: La comida owns the middle of the day, cena is light and late, and eating at six puts you in the room built for tourists
cena: Six in the evening, the fonda is fully lit and empty, and the one open table is a decision about what kind of trip you're having.
decisao: a que horas você come — comer às seis te coloca na sala que só existe pra turista; comer no meio da tarde te coloca na sala em que a cidade de fato almoça
frasePiso: You will walk past a full comedor at two in the afternoon and an empty one at six, and the empty one is the one built for you.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: Typically: desayuno 7:00-10:00, la comida (the main meal) 13:00-15:00, and cena from around 18:00 onward, usually lighter than comida.
fatosDatados.fonte: Consenso de guias gastronômicos convergentes (Mexperience, PanFlavor, Remitly) — não é dado oficial único

steps.pt: Today's decision isn't a phrase — it's a time. What hour you sit down decides which room you eat in.
Good afternoon. Come in, we have a table.
Six in the evening, the whole comedor is yours — every table free, nobody else in the room.
Nothing's wrong. La comida runs one to three — by six, the city already ate. What's open now runs on tourist hours.

steps.pt: Now the other end of the day — cena isn't a second comida, it's later and lighter, sometimes just a stall snack.

The move: want the room the city eats in? Comida, one to three. Just want something before bed? Cena after six, no problem.

aprofundar.titulo: The day has a shape, and it isn't yours yet

secoes.titulo: Three meals, one of them the anchor
secoes.corpo: Desayuno runs morning, comida owns early-to-mid afternoon and is treated as the main event, and cena is later and usually lighter. None of this is a rule enforced anywhere — it's a pattern, and it varies by city and household.

secoes.titulo: An empty room is data, not rejection
secoes.corpo: A restaurant lit up and staffed but empty at six is not failing — it is simply between its two real rushes. Ask when la comida runs if you want the fuller room.

secoes.titulo: Tourist hours exist everywhere they need to
secoes.corpo: Hotel restaurants, airport counters and heavily touristed strips often serve on a schedule closer to what visitors expect. That is a legitimate choice for those places, not a trick — it just isn't the same clock as the neighbourhood fonda.

permissao: You are allowed to eat whenever you're hungry. Nothing here is a rule you can break — comida at six just means you're the only customer instead of one of many, and that's a trade, not a mistake.
espelho: A restaurant back home that's dead at 4pm and slammed at 7pm is running the exact same kind of rhythm — anyone who's ever timed a visit around a lunch rush already understands this instinct; the only new part is that the peak hours themselves have moved.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You walk into a comedor at six in the evening, fully staffed and lit, and it's completely empty except for you.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: This place must not be very good, or something's wrong here.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: La comida, the main meal, typically runs from about one to three in the afternoon — by six, the neighbourhood rush is long over, and the restaurant is simply in its quiet stretch before a lighter evening trade.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: If you want the fuller, livelier room, ask what time comida runs and come back then; if you're just hungry now, an empty room at six is a normal, unremarkable thing to sit down in.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You stop reading an empty room as a red flag and start reading it as a clock.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not in hotel restaurants, airports or heavily touristed strips, which often run on a more continuous schedule geared to visitors rather than the local comida/cena rhythm.
